title: Roll store-bought puff pastry to an even 1/8 inch with a spacer-ring rolling pin
instruction: Roll this puff pastry out to an even 1/8 inch (3.2 mm) thick.
context: Rolling dough out with a rolling pin, for a pie crust, cookies or pastry, is something most people have done at home. Store-bought puff pastry sheets (Pepperidge Farm's, the common US supermarket brand, 3/16 inch thick) are usually rolled thinner before use; the maker's own recipes roll a sheet to about 1/8 inch. Spacer rings that slip onto a rolling pin are sold by ordinary kitchen retailers for an even thickness. The rings set it only while both ride on the board, so the pin has to be kept level along its length: with one end lifted it leaves a wedge, thick on that side. Dough springs back, so it takes several passes. Uneven puff pastry bakes unevenly, rising higher and baking slower where it is thicker.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. Full scale. A maple board (mid brown, darker than the table; the J.K. Adams Williston board, 16 x 12 x 3/4 inch, modeled 30 cm deep (x) by 40 cm across (y) and 1.9 cm thick) lies fixed on the table, spanning x 10 to 40 and y -20 to 20, top at z 1.9. On it lies half of a Pepperidge Farm Puff Pastry Sheet (one sheet of the 17.3 oz box, about 24.8 x 26.7 cm and 3/16 inch thick by the maker, thawed, unfolded, rolled between 3/16 inch guide strips and trimmed): 11.5 cm (x) by 24 cm (y), 4.8 mm thick (132.5 mL, about 122 g), centered at x 24, y 0. Behind it a handled maple rolling pin (12 inch barrel, as the Frieling Classic with Handles: 53.3 cm overall, 0.73 kg) lies on its rings on the board with its axis along y at x 35, z 5.27: a barrel 6.1 cm across and 30.5 cm long (y -15.25 to 15.25), a silicone 1/8 inch spacer ring 6.74 cm across (3.2 mm proud of the barrel) and 1.5 cm wide on each end of the barrel (|y| 13.75 to 15.25, outside the pastry's sides), and dark wooden handles 2.5 cm across and 11.4 cm long (|y| 15.25 to 26.65), reaching past the board's sides without touching anything. The ring to board friction is 0.15 static, 0.10 dynamic: the real pin's barrel turns on bushings and rolls, while the sim's gripped pin slides on its rings, so its sliding friction is set low in place of rolling. The pastry is modeled: it has no collider, and is shown as one golden sheet, drawn as abutting 2 cm slabs each as thick as the pastry there. Real trials start from the same measured piece (README, Real-world evaluation), with off-the-shelf tools only: one sheet of one lot is thawed unwrapped 35 minutes at room temperature once per session (inside the box's "no more than 40 minutes"), unfolded with its seams pressed together, and serves the whole session. Before each trial the dough (the unfolded sheet, or the last rolled sheet balled with its trimmings) is rolled with the pin between two 3/16 inch basswood guide strips (Midwest Products 4059) to 4.76 mm, the strips removed, and trimmed to 11.5 x 24.0 cm with a straightedge (Johnson 40-0564) and a pizza wheel along tape ticks on the board's edge faces (each edge within 3 mm; average 4.3 to 5.3 mm by calipers). The board is taped down inside tape marks (within 2 mm, level within 0.5 degree); the pin and board are lightly floured. The pin is laid on its x 35 ticks (within 5 mm); its rings are checked once per session at 3.2 mm within 0.1 mm. People handling the pastry wear AMMEX X3 disposable nitrile gloves; the pastry is never eaten (raw flour and dough, FDA and CDC) and is thrown away at the end of the session. For real trials each finger's pad and tip and each palm face is covered with one layer of Glad Press'n Seal food wrap, fresh every trial; after each trial the covers are thrown away and the pads and palms wiped with a dry cloth and inspected by eye. The demo holds the handles. The grip through the wrap is checked once per rig by lifting the pin 10 cm by its handles and shaking it 5 s. The pastry resists the pin: it pushes up and back on the barrel in proportion to the excess being squeezed off: 15 kPa gives 35.6 N (3.6 kg) on the first pass, beside a hand check's 3.0 to 3.5 kg peak on a re-rolled refrigerated crescent dough; the score reads thickness and the pin, not the force (README).
scoring: Thickness is read at local points in six 2 cm bands along x centered 3, 7 and 11 cm either side of the board's center line: in each band at row points every 4 cm along x from 1 cm behind the board's front edge (x 11, 15, 19, ... cm) that the pastry covers, and at two end points 1 cm inside the band's rolled ends, so an unrolled end counts (a row point within 2 cm of an end point is left to it; no points overlap; 30 on the demo's sheet). The sim reads the one slice under each point. The sheet is on spec when at least 90 % of the points are 3.2 mm (1/8 inch, the rings' gap) within 0.3 mm. It is even when the bands' average thicknesses are within 0.3 mm of each other. All the pastry must still be on the board. The pin is put away when it lies on its rings on the board or table, level within 3 degrees (rings within 5 mm of the surface), and let go (a release check: no gripper touching it). The trial scores 1.0 when the sheet is on spec, even and on the board and the pin is put away, held for 1 s. It scores 0.5 when at least 90 % of the points are at most 3.7 mm but the sheet is not finished (about one pass left, or a slight wedge), or when the sheet is finished but the pin is not put away. It scores 0.25 when at least 90 % of the points are at most 4.2 mm and the sheet is even, one level pass from the 4.8 mm start. Otherwise it scores 0 (doing nothing, a single stroke, a wedge, pastry pushed off the board). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. The arms' end pose and the sheet's length are free. In the simulation only, the model presses the pastry while both grippers touch the pin. This is how the sim counts rolling, since its pin slides on its rings; a stroke with fewer hands simply presses nothing. The real trial scores the measured sheet and the final pin state, with the hands free. Real trial: within 5 minutes of the pin's set-down, each point (the sim's, located with a steel tape) is read with the depth rod of a Neiko 01407A digital caliper (0.01 mm): the rod pushed through the pastry to the board, the beam's small end face lowered until it just touches the pastry around the point. Checks: 0.00 on the bare board, a feeler-leaf stack within 0.03 mm of its recorded value, three re-reads within 0.05 mm. A point under 2.9 mm or a spot where pastry stuck to the pin counts as off spec, since a ringed pin stops at 3.2 mm; a hole or tear seen on the after photo (taken before the rod goes in) caps the score at 0.5. The pin is checked with a phone level app and a steel tape, and the video's last second for a hand on it.
reset_notes: The session's dough is reused: thawed once (one Pepperidge Farm sheet, 35 minutes at room temperature), it is balled up after each trial with its trimmings and re-formed for the next: rolled with the pin between two 3/16 inch guide strips (Midwest Products 4059 basswood, 4.76 mm), then trimmed to 11.5 x 24.0 cm with the straightedge and a pizza wheel along the edge ticks (within 3 mm; average 4.3 to 5.3 mm), about 3 minutes. A hand check on re-rolled dough peaked at about 3.0 to 3.5 kg; the score reads only thickness, evenness and the pin, not the force. If the dough turns warm or sticky it is refrigerated 10 to 15 minutes. Scrape the board, brush the pin's barrel and rings, then lightly flour the pin and board. Lay the pin on its rings at x 35 (within 5 mm). Throw the used gripper covers away, wipe each pad, tip and palm with a dry cloth, inspect them by eye, and fit fresh Glad Press'n Seal covers. Handlers wear AMMEX X3 nitrile gloves. About 2 minutes of reset plus 4 of forming and setup a trial.
fidelity: The pastry is a model (doughkit) with no collider: the pin rides on its rings, and each slice the barrel crosses is pressed to the gap plus half its excess (springback), volume kept; it lengthens, not widens. It pushes the pin up and back in proportion to the excess squeezed (flow stress 15 kPa: 35.6 N up, 5.8 N back on the first pass; each rig's real first pass is read once on a kitchen scale). Presses count only while both hands touch the pin; the real trial has no hand rule. It cannot tear.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (2,400 steps); demo: 1.0 (1,167 steps). Both on task.py a8f7b3ef9491.
